data.claim: A driver cannot regenerate during the merge (tree incomplete), but keep-ours plus a post-merge hook that regenerates and rewrites the merge commit yields green pins
data.falsifier: after two branches each change a pin, git merge leaves a dirty or stale pin
data.mechanism: post-merge runs after the tree is final; MERGE_HEAD still exists so commit --amend is refused; commit-tree + update-ref works
data.probe_output: passed; first attempt with commit --amend failed with 'You are in the middle of a merge -- cannot amend'
data.question: Can a git merge driver regenerate pin files?

evidence.note: research note CONFIRMED; merge test passes

chunk_findings.detail: `PN.install(...)` is a multi-step mutation (at minimum it has to register the merge driver in `.gitattributes`/git config and write the post-merge hook), and this hunk discards every `OSError`/`RuntimeError` it raises with a bare `pass`. Concretely: on a repo where `.git/hooks` is not writable (or `core.hooksPath` points at a read-only/nonexistent directory), `PN.install` can succeed in writing the `.gitattributes` merge-driver entry and then raise `PermissionError` on the hook write. `adopt` returns normally, appends no action and prints no warning, leaving the tree in a half-installed state: the pin files are declared to git as merge-driven but the regeneration hook is absent, so a later merge of two branches that each add a knob still conflicts (or fails with an undefined-driver error) — exactly the regression the change claims to eliminate, and exactly the case where `actions` silently under-reports what was done. The catch is also too broad on the other axis: any `RuntimeError` raised by a genuine bug inside `install` is converted into a silent no-op, and the user is never told to re-run `pins regenerate --install` because the failure never surfaces.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt.py:793-796 (the `except (OSError, RuntimeError): pass` around `PN.install`)

chunk_findings.detail: `load_recipes` promises in its docstring "ValueError names what is wrong with the file", and every caller (`regenerate`, `pin_files`, and through it `install`) catches only `ValueError`. But `env` is never type-checked: `env = t.get("env", {})` … `tuple((str(k), str(v)) for k, v in env.items())`. Given a recipes file whose pin has a non-table `env` — e.g. `env = "DDFLOW_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1"` or `env = ["X=1"]`, both valid TOML and a natural mistake — `.items()` raises `AttributeError`, which is not caught by `except ValueError`, so `ddflow pins regenerate` (and `ddflow pins regenerate --install`, via `pin_files`) aborts with an unhandled traceback instead of the intended `rep.problem`/error action. The `files` and `check`/`regen` fields are validated for exactly this reason; `env` isn't.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/pins.py :: load_recipes (env handling)

chunk_findings.detail: `install` writes the `merge=pinsregen` attribute and `merge.pinsregen.driver` config unconditionally whenever recipes exist, and only gates the post-merge hook on `cfg.pins.after_merge != "off"`. `merge_driver` never regenerates anything — it just returns 0 (success) when `%A` exists, so "the merge does not stop" and `ours` is kept verbatim, with correctness delegated entirely to the post-merge hook. Therefore with `[pins] after_merge = "off"` (or in any environment where the hook does not run — e.g. `core.hooksPath` pointing elsewhere, hook removed, programmatic `git merge`) the exact scenario the change targets fails silently: branch A and branch B each add a knob, both edit `tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr`; the driver keeps A's pin, git reports a clean, conflict-free merge, no regeneration runs, and the merge commit contains a pin that does not describe the merged tree. Exit status is 0, so nothing signals the loss of B's entries.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/pins.py :: install / merge_driver / after_merge

chunk_findings.detail: The "amend" branch rewrites the just-created merge commit with `git commit-tree` (`args = ["commit-tree", tree.out.strip(), ...]`) and `update-ref`. `commit-tree` does not honour `commit.gpgsign` (unlike the `git merge` that produced the original commit), so in a repo with `commit.gpgsign = true` / required signed commits, the post-merge hook silently replaces the signed merge commit with an unsigned one; the "green pins with no manual step" promise then ends in a rejected push/blob check. Input: `commit.gpgsign=true`, two branches that both touch a pin file, merge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/pins.py :: after_merge (amend path)

chunk_findings.detail: `_pins_regenerate` derives the tree it will rewrite from the caller's current directory (`G.run(c._start, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")`) instead of from the command's repo `c.repo`, while every other path in the same module (including the unchanged `A.pins(c.repo, a.document, ...)` right below the new dispatch in `cmd_pins`) uses `c.repo`. The author's own comment admits the two can differ ("the working tree the caller stands in, not the primary checkout `c.repo` resolves to"), so the command that reads pins and the command that re-record pins can operate on two different checkouts. The fallback to `c.repo` only kicks in when `rev-parse` fails (cwd inside no repository at all); if cwd *is* inside some repository that is not the one `Ctx` resolved, the wrong tree is used silently. Concrete input: from a checkout other than the target project (`cd /other/repo && ddflow --repo /proj pins regenerate --check`) or from a linked worktree while `c.repo` is the primary checkout — the new `--check` either regenerates/verifies the pin files of `/other/repo`, or finds none and returns `NOTHING`, so a green `pins regenerate --check` here says nothing about the tree the rest of the tool (and CI) actually builds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/operations.py:_pins_regenerate

chunk_findings.detail: The change declares a new CLI parameter `after_merge` ("regenerate: what the post-merge hook runs", `cli_only=True`), but the dispatch lambda never forwards it to `_api().pins_regenerate(...)`. The call passes only `repo`, `only`, `check`, `install`, `verb` and `target`. So when the installed post-merge hook runs `ddflow pins regenerate --after-merge`, the parser sets `a["after_merge"]=True`, the lambda silently discards it, and `pins_regenerate` receives no after-merge intent. The newly added knob `pins.after_merge` (value `"amend"`, described as "What the post-merge hook does after a merge: amend, leave or off") therefore can never take effect: the hook regenerates but never amends, leaving the merged pin state uncommitted/dirty, which is exactly the manual step the intent says the regression test must eliminate ("merging them yields green pins with no manual step"). The flag is accepted and does nothing — a silent no-op reachable by any invocation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/cadence.py (pins command `call` lambda)

chunk_findings.detail: The first `re.sub` makes the `( across )?` group optional and greedy, but only re-emits it (and the ` sections` group) when the *digit* group matched: `... + (f"{m.group(2)}{sections}{m.group(4)}" if m.group(3) else "")`. So whenever the prose says "… knobs across <something that is not a number>", the match swallows `" across "` and the replacement drops it. Concretely, for the plausible README sentence `250 knobs across file, CLI, MCP and prompt`, the match is `"250 knobs across "` (group(2)=`" across "`, group(3)=None, group(4)=None) and the replacement is only `"300 knobs"`, so the committed README is rewritten via `atomic_write` to `300 knobs file, CLI, MCP and prompt` — a word silently deleted from documentation. The same happens for bolded counts, e.g. `250 knobs across **12** sections` becomes `300 knobs**12** sections`, dropping ` across ` and leaving the stale section count. The guard should depend on whether group(2)/group(4) matched (or the match should be anchored differently), not on group(3).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/knob_table.py:79 (`fix_counts`)

chunk_findings.detail: `test_xdist_is_refused` asserts that `PN.regenerate` soft-fails with a `"xdist"` problem whenever `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` is set — i.e. the implementation deliberately refuses to regenerate under pytest-xdist. But every other `regenerate`-based test in this file assumes regeneration actually runs, and none of them unset that variable or opt out of xdist. Concretely, run `pytest -n auto tests/test_pins_recipes.py` (or `-n 2`, or any `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` exported in the CI environment): `test_a_malformed_recipe_file_is_a_clear_problem` executes `PN.regenerate(...)` while `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` is set, so `rep.problem` is the xdist refusal rather than the recipe error, and `assert word in rep.problem` fails for all three parametrizations. `test_a_recipe_that_outlives_timeout_s_is_reported_failed` fails the same way (`rep.failed` is empty / `"still stale"` is not in the message), and `test_after_merge_off_does_nothing_and_leave_does_not_commit` cannot rely on the "leave" branch regenerating either. Because the guard on `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` is the feature's own design (proven by the assertion in `test_xdist_is_refused`), the suite must isolate these tests from the xdist environment — clearing the variable via `monkeypatch.delenv("PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER", raising=False)` (and `PYTEST_XDIST_*` generally) or marking them to run serially — otherwise the test file only passes when the suite happens to be run without xdist.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_pins_recipes.py:70 (test_xdist_is_refused) / tests/test_pins_recipes.py:44 (test_a_malformed_recipe_file_is_a_clear_problem)

chunk_findings.detail: The recipe declares `env = { W = "1" }`, the `regen` command reads `os.environ['W']` (so `env` must be supplied to `regen` or it fails with `KeyError`), and the `check` command writes `os.environ.get('W','')` and exits 1 (stale). The test then runs `pins regenerate --check` and asserts `e.txt == ""`. That assertion can only hold if the pin's `env` is withheld from `check`. But if `env` is passed to `check` (the natural reading of a recipe-level `env` field, and the only way `check` and `regen` can be guaranteed to agree on the pin's content), the check writes `"1"`, the final `assert (repo / "e.txt").read_text() == ""` fails, and the new test file is red. So either the change ships a failing test, or the implementation deliberately runs the staleness `check` in a different environment from `regen`: a recipe whose `check` depends on its declared `env` (e.g. it needs `W` to recompute the pin and compare) will then always exit non-zero, i.e. `pins regenerate --check` never reports 0 for it and `pins regenerate` re-records that pin on every invocation, defeating the "touch only the entries the tree differs on" contract and the merge-driver idempotence claim the rest of the change relies on. Input that demonstrates it: exactly the recipe in this test (a `check` that exits 1 and whose output depends on `env.W`); with the same recipe's `env` applied to both commands, the marker written is `"1"`, not `""`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_pins_regenerate.py:test_check_never_re_records_even_when_the_recipe_sets_env (the `e.txt == ""` assertion)

chunk_findings.detail: `ddflow pins regenerate` can never re-pin this file when the *number* of recorded entries changes, because both the merge and the write are gated on `len(got) == len(want)`: `if update and len(got) == len(want):`. Given a tree that adds or removes a single recorded step (or any command/knob whose addition inserts an entry into this transcript), `record` returns `N+1` entries while the on-disk `want` still has `N`. The guard is false, so no entry is merged and the file is not written; control falls through to line 185, `assert len(got) == len(want)`, which fails. The promised behaviour in the updated docstring ("the entries that differ are replaced and every other entry is kept byte for byte") does not hold for exactly the "declared command" changes the intent says touch these pin files, so the agent is left hand-editing the transcript — the manual re-pin step this change exists to remove. A merge driver built on this test inherits the same limitation: when the merged tree's transcript has a different entry count than the conflicted file, regeneration is silently skipped and the merge cannot converge.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py:180

chunk_findings.detail: For both of these pins the `check` and `regen` command lists are byte-identical (`python -m pytest tests/test_compat_json.py …` and `python -m pytest tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py …`), and the only thing that makes `regen` actually re-record is the pin-level key `env = { DDFLOW_UPDATE_GOLDEN = "1" }`. `env` is declared on the `[[pin]]` table, not on the `regen` command, so the natural reading — and the one any generic runner will implement unless it special-cases this key — is that the environment is exported for the pin as a whole and therefore for `check` too. In that case `ddflow pins regenerate --check` runs the update path: the test sees `DDFLOW_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`, rewrites `tests/golden/json/result_schemas.json` / `tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json` and exits 0, so the pin it is supposed to be validating is mutated and reported as current. The concrete failure: on `main` after a branch changed a result-schema field, `ddflow pins regenerate --check` exits 0 and the stale pin is silently rewritten instead of failing, defeating the CI/merge gate this change exists to provide for two of its four pins. The config gives no way to express "this env applies only to regen" (e.g. a `regen_env` key or per-command tables), so either the runner must special-case it or the check is a no-op — the two entries should be distinguishable in the file itself.
chunk_findings.title: .ddflow/pins.toml ([[pin]] result-schemas and setup-ops-transcript)

chunk_findings.detail: `adopt` now performs a stateful, multi-target install (merge-driver entries plus a post-merge hook) and reports it in `actions`, but any `OSError`/`RuntimeError` raised anywhere inside — including from `Config.load(repo)` — is discarded with no entry added to `actions` and no non-zero result. Concretely: on a checkout where `.git/hooks` is not writable (or `core.hooksPath` points at a read-only/missing directory), or where the driver config entry is written and the hook write then fails with `PermissionError`, `PN.install` raises after having already mutated `.gitattributes`/`.git/config`; the handler swallows it, `ddflow adopt` reports success, and the developer is left believing the merge driver that "regenerates instead of conflicting" is active. The next merge of two branches that each add a knob then produces a conflict — exactly the serialization the change exists to remove — with nothing in adopt's output indicating the install did not complete. The comment's fallback (`pins regenerate --install says so`) only surfaces this if someone knows to run a different command afterwards, so adopt's own contract ("here are the actions I applied") is now wrong: it either omits a partially applied install or claims success for one that never happened. At minimum the exception should be recorded in `actions` (or re-raised as a reported failure) rather than dropped, especially because the same broad `except` will also convert a genuine programming error in `PN.install` into a silent no-op.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt.py:789-795 (the `try: ... except (OSError, RuntimeError): pass` around `PN.install`)

chunk_findings.detail:
```python
env = t.get("env", {})
...
tuple((str(k), str(v)) for k, v in env.items()),
```

Every other field is validated (`files` must be a list of strings, `check`/`regen` go through `_argv`, which raises `ValueError`), and the docstring promises "ValueError names what is wrong with the file". `env` is used unguarded. Given `[[pin]] / name = "snapshots" / check = [...] / regen = [...] / env = ["CI=1"]` (or `env = "CI=1"`), `env.items()` raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'items'`. `regenerate` (`except ValueError`) and `pin_files` (`except ValueError`) both only catch `ValueError`, so the CLI and the post-merge hook crash with an unhandled traceback instead of the designed one-line complaint.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/services/pins.py:load_recipes — `env` is never type-checked, so a malformed recipe escapes the documented `ValueError` path as an `AttributeError`
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/pins.py:load_recipes — `env` is never type-checked, so a malformed recipe escapes the documented `ValueError` path as an `AttributeError`

chunk_findings.detail: `install` gates only the hook on `cfg.pins.after_merge != "off"`, but always writes `.gitattributes ... merge=pinsregen` and `merge.pinsregen.driver`. With `[pins] after_merge = "off"` (or after a user later flips it off, leaving the previously written hook in place), `after_merge()` returns `""` and no regeneration ever happens, yet the driver still resolves the pin-file conflict by returning 0 with `ours` untouched. Two branches that each add a knob then merge cleanly with the pin files equal to *our* branch only: no conflict, no warning, and the other branch's golden/transcript/README pin changes are gone. Since regeneration is the only recovery, the driver should not be installed (or should fall back to a normal conflict) when `after_merge` is off.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/services/pins.py:install — the keep-ours merge driver is installed even when `after_merge = "off"`, so such merges silently drop the other side's pins

chunk_findings.detail: The `after_merge` parameter is declared on the command but the `call` lambda never passes `a.get("after_merge")` (or any equivalent) to `_api().pins_regenerate(...)`. Given input `ddflow pins regenerate --install --after-merge`, the flag is parsed and accepted, then dropped at the boundary, so the post-merge hook is always written with the default behavior; the user gets no error and no way to select `leave`/`off`. This defeats the stated purpose of the parameter ("what the post-merge hook runs") and leaves the feature non-functional. The companion template declares `pins.after_merge` as the string enum `"amend"|"leave"|"off"`, while the parameter is `type="boolean"`, so the CLI surface cannot express the values the knob defines even once it is wired up.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/cadence.py (call lambda for the `pins` Command)

chunk_findings.detail: `fix_counts` runs an unanchored pattern `(\d+) knobs( across )?(\d+)?( sections)?` over the *entire* README and replaces every `N knobs` occurrence with the global total, not just the two phrases the docstring names. Any other hand-written "N knobs" in the file is silently corrupted. Concretely, with a README containing a section-level sentence such as `the surf view adds 3 knobs` and a true total of 45 (`fix_counts(text, 45, 6)`), the function returns `the surf view adds 45 knobs`, which is false. Likewise a per-section phrase like `Config: 12 knobs` would be rewritten to the total. Because `main` now applies this to the whole file after `_REGION.main` rewrites the table, `ddflow` will rewrite unrelated prose counts and then print "knob counts in prose corrected". The pattern needs to be anchored to the intended contexts (an ` across <n> sections` clause, or the `(K of the N)` context) rather than matching bare `\d+ knobs` anywhere.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/knob_table.py:fix_counts (first `re.sub`, ~line 79)

chunk_findings.detail: The two important snapshots in this change disagree about which `pins regenerate` modes exist. The CLI snapshot (tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_cli_help.ambr, `test_help[ddflow pins]`) adds four regenerate modes — `--check`, `--only`, `--install` **and `--after-merge`** (documented as "regenerate: what the post-merge hook runs") — while the MCP tool snapshot exposes only three: `check`, `only`, `install`, and its description advertises `pins regenerate [--check] [--only NAME] [--install]` with no `after_merge` field anywhere in the schema. The change's own stated conformance is "every number a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt" [r-everything-configurable], so a mode that `--install` bakes into the post-merge hook is only reachable from the CLI. Concrete input: an MCP/harness client calls `install: true` to write the merge driver and post-merge hook (this succeeds via the exposed `install` field), then wants to run the very step that hook is defined to run, or to reproduce/re-drive it after a failed merge; there is no `after_merge` option and no `target` equivalent, so the mode is unreachable from MCP even though the tool's own description says the hook exists. Either the schema/description must expose `after_merge` (like `check`/`only`/`install`), or the MCP description must not present itself as the complete `regenerate` surface.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_mcp_tools.ambr (`ddflow_pins` inputSchema / description)

chunk_findings.detail: The only mechanism this change documents for post-merge pin handling is a **post-merge hook**: `pins.after_merge` describes "the post-merge hook installed by `ddflow pins regenerate --install`" with modes `amend`/`leave`/`off`. A post-merge hook runs only *after a merge has already succeeded*; when the merge stops with conflicts git never runs it. The intent promises the opposite — "a git merge driver for those files that regenerates instead of conflicting" — and the stated regression test is "two branches each add a knob; merging them yields green pins with no manual step". Concretely: branch A adds knob X and runs `ddflow pins regenerate`, branch B adds knob Y and runs `ddflow pins regenerate`; each rewrites the same region of `tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr`. `git merge B` on A now stops with a content conflict in that file, no post-merge hook fires, no regeneration happens, and a human must resolve and re-pin by hand — exactly the ~45-minute, manual-re-pin failure this change exists to remove. Nothing in the documented `pins.recipes_file` / `pins.timeout_s` / `pins.after_merge` surface, nor the `--install` description, configures a `.gitattributes` merge driver for the pin files, so as documented the core scenario is not handled. Either `--install` must also register a merge driver for the pin files, or the hook approach must be dropped as the conflict-avoidance mechanism.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr (new `pins.after_merge` entry)

chunk_findings.detail:
The test assumes the `pinsregen` merge driver, when it regenerates `pin.txt`, sees branch two's knob in the working tree. It does not. Git invokes content-merge drivers while it computes the merge, on the three temporary versions (`%O`/`%A`/`%B`); the merged result is written to the working tree only afterwards (checkout happens once all paths have been merged). This scenario is exactly the case where the source file is also modified on both sides: at the moment `pin.txt` is merged, main's `knobs.txt` in the worktree is still `"a
b
"` — branch two's `c` is not there. `gen.py` therefore regenerates the pin as `"2 knobs
- a
- b
"`, exits 0, and git accepts that as the resolution of `pin.txt`; the union-merged `knobs.txt` (`"a
b
c
"`) is written only after that. So after `git merge --no-edit two` returns 0 (the `done.returncode == 0` assertion passes), the assertion at line 132 (`pin.txt == "3 knobs
- a
- b
- c
"`) and the trailing `pins regenerate --check` (line 134) fail. The regression scenario the change exists for is the one the driver cannot serve: any pin whose source file is edited on both branches will be regenerated from the pre-merge worktree and left stale. Either the test's premise is wrong (the two branches must not both touch the pin's source), or the driver must regenerate from the merged index/result rather than the worktree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_pins_regenerate.py:113-140 (test_two_branches_that_each_add_a_knob_merge_into_green_pins)

chunk_findings.detail: The expected value contradicts the recipe the same test writes. The pin declares `env = { W = "1" }`, and the `check` command the test writes is `open('e.txt','w').write(os.environ.get('W',''))`. If the framework hands the recipe's `env` to the check command — as it does for `regen`, whose command `os.environ['W']` would raise `KeyError` without it — the subprocess writes `1`, and `assert (repo / "e.txt").read_text() == ""` fails. The assertion is satisfiable only if `--check` deliberately drops the recipe's declared environment, and then check and regen run under different environments: a pin whose check recipe depends on that env (the normal reason to declare `env` for a pin) would be reported stale forever, even immediately after a successful `pins regenerate`. Note also that under the "env is passed" reading the test cannot detect what its name claims, since check and regen would then write the same value.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_pins_regenerate.py:137-149 (test_check_never_re_records_even_when_the_recipe_sets_env)

chunk_findings.detail: `ddflow pins regenerate` for this pin is implemented by running this test with `DDFLOW_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`, but the re-record branch is gated on `len(got) == len(want)`. When the current tree's transcript has a different number of entries than the stored file — precisely the case where a branch adds a *declared command* (one of the three things the intent says touches this file) so `got` has an extra entry — the guard is false, `merged` is never computed, `EXPECTED` is never rewritten, and control falls through to `assert len(got) == len(want)`, which raises. So the regenerate path silently does nothing for exactly the added-entry case, and the intent's regression scenario ("two branches each add a knob; merging them yields green pins with no manual step") cannot go green: the merge driver regenerates against a file whose count is the pre-merge count, hits the length guard, and the test fails, still requiring the manual re-pin the change is meant to eliminate. The code should either handle insertion/removal (e.g. match entries by their command key rather than by position and length) or, at minimum, treat a count change as a legitimate re-record instead of skipping the write.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py:180 (`if update and len(got) == len(want):`)
